goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:74 — Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) check moved from inside the per-event callback to the one-time registerListener call, so if the feature is enabled after the listener registration point the RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent cleanup listener is never installed and orphaned permission resources/policies for removed roles/groups silently persist

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `AdminPermissions.registerListener` changes behavior from always registering the `ProviderEventListener` and gating cleanup per-event (`if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(...))` inside `onEvent`) to only registering the listener when the feature is enabled at registration time (wrapping `manager.register(...)` in the `if`). This does mean that if `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` were to become enabled after `registerListener` is called, no listener would exist to perform the RoleRemoved/GroupRemoved cleanup. Whether that can actually happen (feature flags changing at runtime) is not shown in the diff, so it’s a plausible lifecycle/architecture concern rather than a clearly verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:141 — hasPermission looks up the group's authorization Resource via resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) using the raw group UUID with no type-namespace prefix (unlike V1's "group.resource." prefix), so a resource created for another resource type (e.g. a user) sharing the same id string in the same admin-permissions ResourceServer could be matched instead of the intended group resource

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(), the lookup for a specific group resource is `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, where `groupId` is the raw UUID string. Unlike the existing V1 GroupPermissions naming scheme (`RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX = "group.resource."`), this introduces no namespace/prefix and the lookup is not constrained by resource type, so it relies on an implicit assumption that resource names are globally unique within the admin-permissions ResourceServer across all types (Users/Clients/Groups). The diff does not show such a guarantee, so this is a concrete edge-case/architecture concern (potential cross-type name collision) grounded in the new code, but not definitively provable as an actual defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/UserPermissionsV2.java:105 — Same unprefixed resourceStore.findByName(server, user.getId()) pattern as GroupPermissionsV2, extending the type-collision-by-name risk to users vs. groups/clients sharing the same ResourceServer without type-scoped resource names

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show GroupPermissionsV2 using `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` and AdminPermissionsSchema adding a GROUPS resource type, but it does not show (or change) any `resourceStore.findByName(server, user.getId())` call in `UserPermissionsV2.java` around the cited line. Since the alleged pattern in `UserPermissionsV2` is not present in the provided diff hunks, the finding cannot be verified against this PR diff as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:85 — @AfterEach only removes ScopePermissions (permissions.findAll) but never removes the UserPolicy objects created via createUserPolicy in each test, so policies accumulate across test methods in the same client/realm and could let a later test pass because a policy from a prior test still matches "myadmin" rather than because the code under test is correct

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest`, `@AfterEach` only iterates over and removes `ScopePermissionRepresentation` objects via `permissions.findAll(...).remove()`, but each test also calls `createUserPolicy(...)` to create `UserPolicyRepresentation` objects that are not removed anywhere in this class. That is a diff-grounded test isolation/cleanup concern (leftover policies can accumulate across methods in the same realm/client), even though the claim that they would grant access by themselves is not directly verifiable from the diff because permissions are cleaned up.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/UserPermissionsV2.java:47 — canView(UserModel)/canManage(UserModel) dropped the previous root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.ADMIN, ...) check in favor of only MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS, narrowing rather than widening access, but the inconsistency between V1 and V2 admin-role handling increases the chance a future edit accidentally reintroduces a widening bug

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show UserPermissionsV2 removing `AdminRoles.ADMIN` from the early-return checks in `canView(UserModel)` and `canManage(UserModel)` (now only `MANAGE_USERS`/`VIEW_USERS`). However, the finding’s core concern about an “inconsistency between V1 and V2 admin-role handling” is not supported by this diff: `UserPermissions` (V1) was also changed to use `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS, AdminRoles.VIEW_USERS)` for `canView()` and `AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS` for `canManage()`, i.e., it likewise does not include `AdminRoles.ADMIN`. The remainder of the finding (future widening-bug risk) is speculative and not a concrete, diff-grounded issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:102 — getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel)` was removed and `getGroupsWithViewPermission()` renamed to `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` on a public interface, breaking any external implementer/caller (e.g. admin REST extensions modeled on rest/admin-ui-ext) at compile time with no deprecation cycle

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a source/binary incompatible change to the public interface `GroupPermissionEvaluator`: the method `getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel group)` is removed entirely, and `getGroupsWithViewPermission()` is replaced by `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` (see `GroupPermissionEvaluator.java`). While this PR updates in-repo call sites (e.g., `UsersResource`, `BruteForceUsersResource`) and implementations (`GroupPermissions`, new `GroupPermissionsV2`), any external implementer or caller of this interface would fail to compile without a deprecation/transition path. That’s a concrete API-compatibility concern introduced by the diff, though not necessarily a runtime defect in this repo.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissions.java:267 — canList() reordered to `root.hasOneAdminRole(...) || canView()` from `canView() || hasOneAdminRole(...)`; purely stylistic since both are pure/side-effect-free boolean checks and || is commutative, so this is unnecessary diff noise but harmless.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `canList()`, but it is not merely a commutative reorder of `A || B`. It also changes the explicit admin-role check from `hasOneAdminRole(VIEW_USERS, MANAGE_USERS, QUERY_GROUPS)` to only `hasOneAdminRole(QUERY_GROUPS)`, relying on the updated `canView()` implementation (now `hasOneAdminRole(MANAGE_USERS, VIEW_USERS)`) to cover the other roles. So the finding mischaracterizes the change as purely stylistic reorder-only noise; it’s a small refactor with equivalent intent, not a review issue grounded in “unnecessary reorder”.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:91 — testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers grants only VIEW_MEMBERS and asserts the user becomes visible, but never asserts that VIEW_MEMBERS alone still forbids managing/updating that user, so scope-granularity (view vs manage) between VIEW_MEMBERS and MANAGE_MEMBERS is never actually verified as a negative case

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers`, the test creates a permission granting only `VIEW_MEMBERS` and then asserts that the admin can now *see* Alice via `users().search(...)`. Unlike `testCanViewUserByManageGroupMembers`, it does not include any assertion that updating/managing Alice remains forbidden after granting only `VIEW_MEMBERS`. Given the diff introduces/changes scope-based behavior distinguishing `VIEW_MEMBERS` vs `MANAGE_MEMBERS` (e.g., `GroupPermissions(V2).canViewMembers` allows `VIEW_MEMBERS` or `MANAGE_MEMBERS`, while manage actions depend on `MANAGE_MEMBERS`), the absence of a negative case leaves scope granularity (view-only not implying manage) unverified for this new logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:284 — testManageGroupMembership grants both an all-users MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP permission and a group-level MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP permission simultaneously before asserting joinGroup succeeds, so it cannot tell which permission (or the combination) is actually responsible for granting access; no isolation of MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP alone, no negative case with only one of the two granted

adjudication.rationale: In GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest#testManageGroupMembership, the test grants both an all-users permission (createAllUserPermission(policy, Set.of(MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP))) and a group-level permission (createGroupPermission(topGroup, Set.of(MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP), policy)) before asserting that joinGroup succeeds for bob. Because both permissions are enabled at the same time, the test does not isolate whether MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP alone, MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP alone, or only their combination is required for the operation, and it lacks corresponding negative/positive cases to disambiguate the intended authorization behavior.
